# Rating study a4-v2: expected interval half-widths

Simulated, not measured: no a4-v2 rating exists yet. The set holds the grader's verdicts right : close : wrong = 1 : 1 : 1, so a third of the pairs are passes (task success). Each rater does 27 pairs; every pair gets two raters before a new one opens; the set has 300 pairs. Two cases for how often people call a pair "same" given the grader's verdict, and two for how often two raters split. Every half-width is multiplied by 1.199 for pairs sharing a task (the factor measured on a4-v1). 4000 simulated studies per cell.

## If people nearly always agree with the grader

People say "same" on 97% of the grader's passes and on 3% of its fails.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| 10 | 135 | 45 | ±0.10 to ±0.11 (≈0.82) | ±0.08 to ±0.09 (≈0.92) | ±0.13 to ±0.17 | above 6% |
| 15 | 202 | 67 | ±0.08 to ±0.09 (≈0.82) | ±0.06 to ±0.08 (≈0.92) | ±0.11 to ±0.14 | above 4% |
| 22 | 297 | 99 | ±0.07 (≈0.82) | ±0.05 to ±0.06 (≈0.92) | ±0.09 to ±0.11 | above 3% |

## If the grader is off about one time in ten

People say "same" on 90% of the grader's passes and on 10% of its fails.

| raters finishing | pairs with 2 raters | of them passes | kappa, grader vs people | grader's passes confirmed | people vs people (Fleiss) | false-pass rate ruled out if no pass is contradicted |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 67 | 22 | ±0.19 to ±0.20 (≈0.69) | ±0.16 (≈0.86) | ±0.18 to ±0.24 | above 13% |
| 10 | 135 | 45 | ±0.13 to ±0.14 (≈0.69) | ±0.11 (≈0.86) | ±0.13 to ±0.17 | above 6% |
| 15 | 202 | 67 | ±0.11 (≈0.69) | ±0.09 (≈0.86) | ±0.10 to ±0.14 | above 4% |
| 22 | 297 | 99 | ±0.09 (≈0.69) | ±0.07 to ±0.08 (≈0.86) | ±0.09 to ±0.12 | above 3% |

Ranges cover two raters splitting on 10% and on 20% of pairs. Unweighted, per rating, raters taken as alike: the weighted numbers and a panel of raters who differ will be wider. The last column is exact (1 - 0.05^(1/n) for n passes), before the task factor.
